new_statements.quote: Ударение, как правило, падает на последний слог слова: ossoxū́n 'кость', tårīkī́ 'темнота', vašä́ 'голодный', pürä́ 'мальчик, сын', bugǻ 'отец', muné 'мать' и т. д. Исключения немногочисленны. Не принимают на себя ударение приименные постпозитивные элементы: 1) изафетный показатель: ǰän-e siå 'черная женщина', dúss-e mæhrebū́n-e hamā́ 'наш добрый друг', mǻr-e ziå̄d 'много змей'; 2) показатель неопределенности -(y)e: ǰä́ne 'какая-то (одна) женщина', kū́he 'какая-то (одна) гора' ...; 3) энклитические местоимения (местоименные энклитики): xar-aš 'его голова', ... gūš-am 'мое ухо', dox-aš 'его дочь'.
new_statements.translation: Stress, as a rule, falls on the last syllable of the word: ossoxún 'bone', tårīkí 'darkness', vašá 'hungry', pürá 'boy, son', bugǻ 'father', muné 'mother', etc. Exceptions are few. The adnominal postpositive elements do not take stress: 1) the ezafe marker: ǰän-e siå 'black woman', dúss-e mæhrebún-e hamá 'our good friend', mǻr-e ziåd 'many snakes'; 2) the indefiniteness marker -(y)e: ǰä́ne 'some (one) woman', kúhe 'some (one) mountain' ...; 3) the enclitic pronouns: xar-aš 'his head', ... gūš-am 'my ear', dox-aš 'his daughter'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of the word (stem plus stress-bearing suffixes such as plural/definite markers); enclitics (ezafe -e, indefinite -e/-i, pronominal clitics, object -rā) fall outside the stress domain and are unstressed. In verbs stress sits on the personal ending unless a modal/aspectual prefix, preverb or the negative is present, which then attracts the (main) stress (Christensen 1930 §§11-12; Rastorgueva & Molchanova 1999 p. 177).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Christensen 1930 (p. 36) marks only primary accent and says secondary-accent rules are as in literary Persian; for Natanzi verbs with an infixed pronominal clitic he hears 'deux accents presque également forts', one on the prefix and one on the ending/stem (p. 247 §11). Moshkalo says nothing on secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Исключения немногочисленны' (few lexical exceptions, not listed). Unstressed: ezafe, indefinite article, enclitic pronouns, -rā; Yarandi/Natanzi determinative -a stressed (in Natanzi only before relative ke, Christensen p. 247). In gender-retaining Natanzic varieties the feminine marker is an unstressed -a, giving penultimate stress on feminine nouns (Abyāneʾi bā́la 'spade', kárga 'hen'; Natanzi kárga — Yarshater 1983, Borjian 2012). Verbs: prefixes/preverbs and negation attract stress; compound tenses stress the auxiliary (Christensen p. 247).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule stated on citation forms from Christensen's 1929 text transcriptions (Farizandi, Yarandi); Christensen notes that accentuation of function words 'dépend quelquefois de la diction' (phrase-level). Christensen's own first-hand formulation for Farizandi/Yarani is 'en général les mêmes qu'en persan' (p. 132) and for Natanzi proper 'diffèrent à peine de celles du färizändī et du yaranī' (p. 247).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is from Moshkalo's entries on Farizandi (Glottolog fari1234) and Yarandi (yara1255), two daughter varieties of Natanzic (nata1252); the underlying data are Christensen's 1929 field texts. Christensen 1930 p. 247 states first-hand that Natanzi proper (nata1257, dialect of the town of Natanz, informant from Natanz via Tehran) 'hardly differs' in accentuation from Farizandi/Yarani, whose accent principles are 'in general the same as in Persian'. For the gender-retaining members (Abyāneʾi abya1234; also Natanzi per Borjian's 'Nat kárga'), feminine nouns carry an unstressed final -a (penultimate stress) per Yarshater 1983 and Borjian 2012.

sources.note: No general word-stress rule. Morpheme-level: indefinite -e/-i unstressed (Aby (ya) rū-e 'one day'); definite -a/-e 'stressed, as in colloquial Persian' (Aby kāši-a); feminine marker is 'an unstressed -a' (Del, Aby bā́la 'spade'; Nat kárga 'hen')—i.e. penultimate stress on feminine nouns in gender-retaining Natanz-area varieties.

sources.note: PRIMARY. p. 132 §11 (Färizändi & Yarani, 'Accentuation'): 'Les principes de l'accentuation dans les deux dialectes sont en général les mêmes qu'en persan.' Suffix -íkä attracts accent; determinative -ä/-e/-æj accented or not 'selon la diction'; pronominal suffixes unaccented; §12 (p. 132-133) verbs: accent generally on the ending (last syllable of a polysyllabic ending, except 3sg fem -éā); prefixes/preverbs bä, a, hā, dar, vā etc. attract accent; negation takes accent over other prefixes; §13 unaccented: relative ke, conjunctions, prepositions, postposition -de. p. 247 §10 (Natanzi proper):…

sources.citation: Ivanov, Vladimir B. 2022. Tekye dar guyeš-e abyanei [Stress in the Abyane'i dialect]. In: Pažuhešhā-yi dar bāre-ye kerānehā-ye daryā-ye Kāspiyan [Studies on the coasts of the Caspian Sea], daftar 7, pp. 47-49. Tehrān: Pežvāk-e Farzān. ISBN 978-600-8991-44-1. (In Persian.)
sources.note: Describes another variety. Acoustic study of word stress: F0 follows sentence intonation, not the stressed syllable, so word prominence is not pitch-based; stress cued by duration x intensity. Lexical tone never raised as such.

tone.quote: لحن و تکیه در بیشتر موارد مطابق با آن عمل میکردند، یعنی هجای تکیهدار در آن بخش از ساختار زبانی قرار میگرفت که در آن لحن بالا میرفت. ... تأثیر لحن بر تُن غالب بود (p=0،05، نگ. جدول 1) و در این مورد F0 هجای تکیهدار کمتر از هجای بدون تکیه بود. بنابراین، چنین نتیجهگیری شد که تکیه در گویش ابیانهای تونیك نیست. ... با اصلاح نتیجۀ مطالعۀ قبلی (ایوانف 2011)، تکیه در گویش ابیانهای را میتوان به شکل مقداریـپویا (quantitative-dynamic) طبقهبندی کرد.
tone.locator: p. 49, paragraph above Table 1 and closing paragraph
tone.translation: Intonation and stress in most cases acted in agreement, i.e. the stressed syllable fell in that part of the structure where the intonation rose. ... The effect of intonation on pitch was dominant (p=0.05, see Table 1), and in this case the F0 of the stressed syllable was lower than that of the unstressed syllable. Therefore it was concluded that stress in the Abyane'i dialect is not tonic. ... correcting the result of the earlier study (Ivanov 2011), stress in the Abyane'i dialect can be classified as quantitative-dynamic.

tone.summary: No tones described. Word stress analysed acoustically: cues = vowel duration (primary) + F0 maximum (secondary), intensity not significant in disyllables; integral intensity significant in the larger vowel sample; intonation effects exceed stress effects. Pitch functions as a stress correlate, not as lexical tone. Stress position not stated in this source.
